observation_summary: The method DiscreteDistribution.sample(int) throws an ArrayStoreException because it attempts to create an array using the class of the first element in the list, which may not be a supertype of all elements returned by the sampling process.
reasoning_summary: The defect lies in the procedural logic used to instantiate the result array. The code assumes that the class of the first element in the list is a valid type for all elements in the array, which is an incorrect algorithmic assumption for generic collections. This is a local procedural error in how the array is initialized, not a missing guard (Checking) or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object).
evidence_used: Bug report description: Creating an array with Array.newInstance(singletons.get(0).getClass(), sampleSize) in DiscreteDistribution.sample(int) is risky.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While it involves type compatibility, the root cause is the internal implementation logic of the sample method, not a mismatch in the interface contract between two components.
The class and method exist and are intended to perform this task; the implementation strategy for array creation is simply flawed.
